stem: A client with a clinical condition associated with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) has a fibrinogen result within the laboratory reference interval. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: A normal fibrinogen result by itself rules out DIC.
options.B: DIC can be diagnosed only when fibrinogen is below the reference interval.
options.C: A normal fibrinogen result alone does not rule out DIC; the diagnosis depends on the clinical setting and the overall coagulation pattern, including platelet count, PT/aPTT, fibrin-related markers, and fibrinogen.
options.D: Fibrinogen has no role in evaluating suspected DIC.

rationale: NCBI StatPearls states that no single history, examination, or laboratory component can diagnose or rule out DIC. Evaluation uses the clinical context together with a pattern of laboratory findings such as platelet count, PT/aPTT, fibrin-related markers, and fibrinogen. A decreased fibrinogen level can support DIC, but a fibrinogen result within the reference interval cannot by itself exclude the diagnosis. C is therefore the most accurate interpretation.
educational_objective: Avoid excluding DIC on the basis of one normal fibrinogen result; interpret fibrinogen as one component of the clinical and laboratory pattern used to evaluate suspected DIC.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf)
source_version_date: Last update May 1, 2024; StatPearls 2026 edition; accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: Evaluation — no single history, physical examination, or laboratory component can diagnose or rule out DIC; laboratory pattern includes PT, aPTT, fibrinogen, platelet count, schistocytes, and fibrin-related markers
source_claim_supported: No single laboratory component, including fibrinogen, can rule out DIC; evaluation requires the clinical setting and a pattern of coagulation findings.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed p.13, Reduction of Risk Potential — review laboratory results and recognize complications/risk patterns
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — DIC laboratory interpretation

source_original.stem: A client with suspected disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) has a fibrinogen value that is still within the reference range. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: A normal fibrinogen value reliably excludes disseminated intravascular coagulation from consideration
options.B: Fibrinogen must be profoundly reduced at presentation for disseminated intravascular coagulation
options.C: Fibrinogen may fall with consumption, but a normal or elevated value does not exclude DIC
options.D: Fibrinogen has no useful role when evaluating suspected disseminated intravascular coagulation

source_original.rationale: DIC consumes platelets and coagulation factors, and fibrinogen can decrease as consumption progresses. However, fibrinogen is also an acute-phase reactant and may remain normal or elevated, especially earlier in the process. A normal fibrinogen value therefore does not exclude DIC; diagnosis relies on the clinical setting and a pattern of serial coagulation findings.
source_original.source_detail: Evaluation/pathophysiology: consumptive coagulopathy can reduce fibrinogen, but laboratory diagnosis uses a pattern and fibrinogen may not be low early; last update 2024, accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed the unsupported source-specific assertion that fibrinogen may remain elevated because it is an acute-phase reactant; the final item relies on the directly supported rule that no single laboratory value can rule out DIC and that fibrinogen is interpreted within a broader pattern. Difficulty reduced from hard to medium.

audit_findings.currentness: NCBI chapter updated 2024-05-01 and published in StatPearls 2026 edition.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final claim is limited to what the source explicitly supports: no single lab can rule out DIC and fibrinogen is one part of the diagnostic laboratory pattern.

distractor_audit.B: Overstates fibrinogen as mandatory for diagnosis.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because fibrinogen is part of established DIC scoring/evaluation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C correctly balances the role and limitation of fibrinogen without claiming it is irrelevant or decisive alone.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are interpretations of the same laboratory result; no unrelated mechanism distractors remain.
audit_findings.blueprint: Reduction of Risk Potential is appropriate for interpretation of laboratory findings in a high-risk complication.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the NCBI Evaluation section, rejected the original acute-phase/elevated-fibrinogen explanation because it was not directly supported by that source, rebuilt the rationale around the no-single-test rule, and confirmed C remained uniquely correct.
